about: The priest signs himself and begins the Mass with In nómine Patris. The antiphon “Introíbo ad altáre Dei” comes from Ps 42:4 in the Vulgate (Ps 43:4 in Hebrew numbering). It precedes the psalm from which it is taken and is repeated after the psalm ends.

s01.narrative: The vested priest approaches the altar, makes the reverence due to it, signs himself from forehead to breast and speaks aloud.

s02.translation: In the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit. Amen.

s03.narrative: With hands joined before his breast, the priest begins the antiphon.

narrative_citations.title: Missale Romanum (1962)
narrative_citations.locator: Ordo Missae rubric before Introibo ad altare Dei

s04.translation: I will go in unto the altar of God.

s05.translation: To God, who gladdens my youth.

w003.function: Genitive depending on “nómine” (w002), parallel to “Fílii” (w005) and “Spíritus” (w007).

w007.function: “Spíritus” can be nominative or genitive. Agreement with “Sancti” (w008) establishes the genitive here.

w012.function: Accusative governed by “ad” (w011), which expresses direction.

w016.function: Nominative as the subject of “lætíficat” (w017), although its antecedent “Deum” (w015) is accusative.

w018.function: The Latin “youth” corresponds to the Greek text of the psalm. The Hebrew text speaks here of joy.
